title: restic prune fails and reports missing data
body: I am using restic 0.18.1 on Linux with a version 1 repository on Backblaze B2. Running `restic prune` for a repository with 170 snapshots stops after reporting many pack files that are not found in the index, says data seems to be missing, and exits with `Fatal: index is not complete`. Before this, I used `repair snapshots --forget` and `rewrite --forget` on snapshots originally created with restic 0.12. I had also interrupted an attempt to repair all snapshots because it went silent for a long time. A smaller repair/rewrite/prune test had completed successfully. I want to repair the repository so prune can run safely.

symptoms_visible: When I run `restic prune`, it lists many data packs as not found in the index, says data seems to be missing, refuses to start pruning, and exits with `Fatal: index is not complete`.
N0.label: N0 prune refuses incomplete repository

symptoms_visible: My check output contains `unexpected file size` errors for two pack files and errors while reading content referenced by three trees.
N1.label: N1 check identifies repository damage

symptoms_visible: After running the pack repair, a new check no longer lists the two unexpected-size pack files, but it still prints errors for missing content referenced by trees.
N2.label: N2 damaged packs removed, tree errors remain

symptoms_visible: `restic repair index` processes 236 indexes, deletes one old index, and prints `done`.
I cannot find the named 40-hex-digit files on my computer and suspect they were old Mozilla cache entries.
N3.label: N3 index rebuilt

symptoms_visible: `restic repair snapshots --forget` reports that missing content was removed from snapshot files under my Firefox `cache2/entries` directory.
N4.label: N4 damaged snapshots repaired

symptoms_visible: `restic prune` and `restic check` now run cleanly; prune completes and reclaims about 2% of the repository.
N_terminal.label: terminal repository repaired and verified

question_patterns: Please run `restic check --verbose=2` and share the complete output.
What does a verbose repository check report before we attempt any repair?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I ran it and attached the full output. The check includes `unexpected file size` lines for packs `f3ade64cdd31ea7697ad1a9831a09d7e2f93df83f526e68c025f66d7791f3acd` and `1ed8c1dd8c0f0035279b17f0b1476fab2303830857f60de55d725ed80f7404e1`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The verbose check ends with `no errors were found` and contains no unexpected-size pack files or tree errors.
The same two unexpected-size pack errors appear, but the check was run without verbose level 2.

question_patterns: Does the check output also name any damaged trees or missing blobs?
Please include the tree errors from the check output.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. The output reports missing content referenced from trees beginning `8a2d9c58`, `a37e0905`, and `f63d7a88`; one full tree ID shown is `f63d7a881a585ff2681b0a62f991328c2e280db3a96faa42ec72eee486177cad`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: There are only index errors; the check reports no damaged trees and no missing blob content.

question_patterns: How large is the repository? Please run `restic stats --mode debug`.
Can you share the debug statistics for the repository?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I attached that output too. The repository is nearly 3 TiB, with about 16 GiB of tree metadata.

edges.comment: Comments c0-c2, reporter's repository: participant1 requested verbose check and debug statistics; the reporter supplied the command outputs. The pack and tree identifiers are raw lines from that evidence, while their cause is interpreted on the next edge.

question_patterns: After applying the recommended repair, please rerun `restic check` and tell me whether the two pack-file errors remain.
Can you run another repository check after that command and share what it reports?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I reran `restic check`. The output no longer contains the errors for the two repaired pack files.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The repeat check still reports the same unexpected sizes for both pack files.

question_patterns: What errors, if any, remain in the new check output?
Does the repeat check still report missing content in any trees?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The new check still prints errors for missing blobs referenced by the damaged trees, including tree `f63d7a88`; I attached the complete log.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The repeat check ends with `no errors were found`; no tree or missing-content errors remain.
The two pack errors are gone and the same tree errors remain, but the order of the tree messages differs.

solution.intent: Repair the two malformed pack files named by `restic check`, preserving any intact blobs while removing the damaged packs, and then reassess the remaining repository errors.
solution.concrete_example: Run `restic repair packs f3ade64cdd31ea7697ad1a9831a09d7e2f93df83f526e68c025f66d7791f3acd 1ed8c1dd8c0f0035279b17f0b1476fab2303830857f60de55d725ed80f7404e1`, keep the generated local pack files until the repair is settled, and rerun `restic check`.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the check lines. Maintainers inferred that interrupting `repair snapshots` could at worst leave garbage and did not cause this damage, and that the oversized-pack/incomplete-index state most likely originated under a much older restic version.

edges.comment: Comments c2, c4-c7, reporter's repository: participant1 and participant2 recommended the pack repair printed by check. The reporter ran it, uploaded its output and generated files, and then supplied a second check showing that the pack errors were gone while tree-content errors remained.

solution.intent: Rebuild the repository index from the surviving pack headers before attempting snapshot repair.
solution.concrete_example: Run `restic repair index`. It rebuilds index information from the repository packs and must complete before `restic repair snapshots --forget` is used.

edges.comment: Comments c2, c5, c8-c10, reporter's repository: support explained that snapshot repair requires a correct index. The reporter then ran `restic repair index`, which processed 236 indexes, deleted one old index, and ended with `done`.

solution.intent: Repair the snapshots against the rebuilt index and forget the broken originals, accepting removal of content that is genuinely absent from the repository.
solution.concrete_example: After the index repair completes, run `restic repair snapshots --forget` and allow it to scan the repository. Its output should identify paths whose missing content was removed from the replacement snapshots.

edges.comment: Comments c9-c13, reporter's repository: after rebuilding the index, the reporter ran snapshot repair. Its own output mapped a previously missing 40-character name to a path under `.cache/mozilla/firefox/.../cache2/entries`, confirming that the discarded content was old cache data.

solution.intent: Preview pruning after the pack, index, and snapshot repairs, then perform the real prune and verify repository integrity with a clean check.
solution.concrete_example: First run a verbose prune dry run such as `restic prune -nvv`. If the plan is sensible and no integrity error appears, run the real `restic prune`, then run `restic check` and report whether both commands complete cleanly.

edges.comment: Comments c13-c14, reporter's repository: support recommended a verbose prune dry run before pruning in earnest. The reporter later confirmed that both the real prune and `restic check` completed cleanly and that prune reclaimed about 2%.

satisfaction_conditions: Must diagnose the case as pre-existing pack/index damage in an old version 1 repository: verbose check exposed two malformed pack files and missing content referenced by three trees; maintainers considered the damage likely to predate restic 0.18.1.
Must not blame the interrupted `restic repair snapshots` run for corrupting the repository; the thread establishes that interruption may leave garbage but does not damage existing repository data.

Must not claim that source files disappearing during an ordinary backup caused this repository corruption; the unrecoverable paths were old Firefox cache entries, while the pack/index damage was considered much older.
Must follow the safe repair order established by the evidence: repair the two damaged packs, rerun check, rebuild the index, then repair and forget broken snapshots before pruning.
Must not advise forcing or repeatedly retrying prune while the index is incomplete, because prune intentionally refuses to proceed to prevent additional data loss.
Must ask the reporter to verify the result by running the real prune and a subsequent repository check, and must treat the issue as resolved only after both run cleanly.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced command-line backup user but not a restic internals expert; can run exact diagnostic and repair commands, preserve logs, and inspect paths, but is uncomfortable compiling custom code or interpreting binary pack files.
persona_hint.communication_style: Polite, careful, and detailed. Shares full command output, asks before destructive steps, openly states uncertainty, and reports progress promptly with concrete excerpts.
